01 / ABOUTA LITTLE ABOUT ME

Curious by nature.
Hands-on by choice.

I’m Jerow A. Amelo, a fourth-year Computer Engineering Technology undergraduate at the Technological University of the Philippines Visayas.

My work spans ESP32 and Arduino systems, sensor integration, circuit design, and web applications. I enjoy connecting physical devices to software that makes information easier to understand and use.

Alongside engineering projects, I manage social media and promotional content for Adriano’s, bringing a creative perspective to the way I build and communicate.

03 / KEY PROJECT & THESISLEADING A CONNECTED CAMPUS PROJECT

AquaWatch.
From sensing to status.

An IoT-enabled water dispenser management system developed for the Technological University of the Philippines Visayas.

Project & Thesis Leader

Connecting the hardware,
the team, and the campus.

I led the AquaWatch thesis project, bringing together load-cell sensing, ESP32 monitoring nodes, a physical LED campus map, and a web platform.

Two weighing units estimate remaining water from calibrated weight readings. Their data travel over Wi-Fi to a cloud database, where the web dashboard and a separate ESP32-powered campus display retrieve the latest dispenser status.

ESP32HX711Load-cell sensingCalibrationRGB indicatorsIoT
See the web dashboard

Tested as a complete system.

Controlled prototype testing across two monitoring nodes: 10 trials per test, with 50 observations across five tests.

Mean absolute weight error
8.00 g
Mean transmission latency
1.64 s
Correct status classifications
10 / 10 trials

Results apply to the controlled tests documented in our thesis. Live operation depends on calibration, stable loading, power, and internet connectivity.
